Critical Power & W′ Calculator

Enter two or three all-out efforts to get your Critical Power and W′ (W prime), and see the power you can hold for any effort from 2 to 20 minutes.

Your two efforts

Use maximal efforts, fully paced, ideally on the same day with at least 30 minutes easy riding between them, or on fresh days. 3 and 12 minutes work well; a third effort (for example 7 minutes) makes the result more reliable.

How it works

WHAT CRITICAL POWER AND W′ TELL YOU

Critical Power (CP) is the highest power you can sustain for a long time without your fatigue running away. It sits close to your FTP, but it comes from more than one effort, so it describes you better.

W′ (W prime) is your energy above Critical Power, in kilojoules: a battery you use every time you go over CP, in an attack, a climb or a sprint, and that recharges when you ride below it. Two riders with the same CP can race very differently because of their W′.

How the calculation works

The work you do in each effort is power × time. Plotting work against time for your efforts gives a straight line: its slope is your Critical Power and the point where it starts is your W′. From those two numbers we can predict your best power for any effort from about 2 to 20 minutes.

Get reliable numbers

The result is only as good as your efforts: they must be truly all-out and well paced. Our coaching uses Critical Power and W′ with Vekta to set your training zones and track your fatigue.
